clue.text: Sees, around drunk youngster, frozen drinks

indicators.note: the word for sees is placed around the other two pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to see someone is to spy them, so sees gives spies
a lush is a habitual drunk
a pup is a young dog, or a cheeky youngster

explanation.surface: Someone notices a drunken young person and some frozen drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Slush Puppies are a brand of flavoured crushed-ice drink, sold to children in Britain and elsewhere.

clue.text: Desolate year existed in past

indicators.note: the year and existed pieces go in the word for past

parts.note: late means past, as in the late king
was means existed

explanation.surface: A bleak year that existed long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: To desolate a place is to devastate it, ravage and ruin it.

clue.text: Place in faculty announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word sounds like the one heard

parts.note: sight is one of the five faculties or senses

explanation.surface: A position in a university department is made public.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position where something stands.

clue.text: £25 pens used, fancy writing false names

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the money word holds the anagram

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: fancy as in elaborately reworked, so the letters of used are rearranged

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Twenty-five pounds' worth of second-hand pens produce fancy fake signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudonyms are assumed names used instead of a real one, such as pen names.

clue.text: Monarch's occupying soldiers held Austin?

indicators.note: the monarch occupies, sits inside, the word for captured soldiers

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war, soldiers held captive
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A king's troops have imprisoned someone called Austin.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin Powers is the spoof spy played by Mike Myers, so Austin is an example of someone with this surname.

clue.text: Dramatist is describing individual officer

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing around, so is surrounds the individual

parts.note: one means a single individual
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A playwright portrays a particular military officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was the Romanian-French playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd, author of Rhinoceros.

clue.text: Relation finds right time to be stuck in traffic

indicators.note: the right and time pieces are stuck in the trade word

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, so traffic gives selling
a Tory is right-wing

explanation.surface: A relative discovers the right moment to get caught in a jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Relation here means a narration or account, the telling of a tale.

clue.text: 22's business dynasty

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the arrival at 22, read as a noun

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
the Ming dynasty ruled China 1368-1644

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue's commercial empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer at 22 means arrival, and an arrival is an approach or appearance.

clue.text: Old mail service's curse about NYE crowd

indicators.note: the curse word goes about, that is around, the three printed letters

parts.note: pox is an old curse, as in 'a pox on you'
a press is a dense crowd, as in the press of people

explanation.surface: A historic postal firm swears at a New Year's Eve crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: NYE, the usual short form for New Year's Eve, is not converted into anything: its three letters go straight into the curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pony Express was the American horseback mail relay of 1860-61, now long gone.

clue.text: Take faulty present back then study martial art

indicators.note: faulty letters are wrong as arranged, so the word take is rearranged
back means the word for present is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: present as in the current time is now
to do a subject is to study it, as in 'she does French'

explanation.surface: Return a defective gift, then go and learn a combat sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean combat sport built on kicks, one of the best-known martial arts.

clue.text: Hanger-on the leaders butcher?

definitions.meaning: a hanger-on trails after an army or a cause
butcher read as more butch, the opposite of camp, and leaders the opposite of followers, so the phrase describes the reverse

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the person clinging on is the leaders' meat supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is an opposites joke: 'butcher' as more butch is the antonym of camp, and leaders are the antonym of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian trailing an army, or an uncommitted supporter of a group, fits a dependent who tags along.

clue.text: Sort of thing covering wheels

indicators.note: something that wheels turns round, so the word for covering faces the other way

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate covering something

explanation.surface: Describes some kind of item that sits over a set of wheels, like a car cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of thing' is the definition, as in asking what animal a thing is.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially an animal is a kind or type of thing, as in 'a different animal altogether'.

clue.text: New Year is over in Russia — yes, probably

indicators.note: the anagram goes over, covering, the Russian word on either side
new means the letters of year is are freshly arranged

parts.note: da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: The new year has ended in Russia, and probably someone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is likely, one hedges with this phrase, so it stands for probably or presumably.

clue.text: See work, or hear drunk's verbosity

parts.note: lo means see or behold
go means work or function

indicators.note: drunk as in reeling, so or hear is jumbled

explanation.surface: Look at the workings, or listen to a drunk rambling on.
explanation.definitionFit: Logorrhoea is excessive wordiness, talking far too much.

clue.text: Body of water in drum — uniform gets put inside

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the word for drum, which encloses them

parts.note: to pound is to drum or beat
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A uniform ends up inside a drum full of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Puget Sound is a large inlet of the Pacific in Washington State, around Seattle.

clue.text: Sink full when wife's left

indicators.note: left as in departed: the wife's letter has gone away

parts.note: whole means full or entire

explanation.surface: A sink is full now that the wife has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf and snooker, to sink a ball is to put it in the cup or pocket, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Posh kid put up with playing regularly

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of playing is taken

explanation.surface: A wealthy youngster is tolerated while playing at set intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh is Victoria Beckham, once Posh Spice of the Spice Girls; Brooklyn is her eldest son.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn Beckham is the eldest son of former Spice Girl 'Posh' Victoria Beckham.

clue.text: No more balls

definitions.meaning: no more means finished or ended
in cricket six balls bowled in succession make up one set from one end

explanation.surface: Someone declares an end to ball games, or something cheekier.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished is the first sense; the cricket term for a sequence of six deliveries is the second.

clue.text: See 9
Fuel stocks start to make crime sadly profitable

indicators.note: a store stocks goods, holding them within, so the fuel word contains the rest

parts.note: coal is a fuel

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word
sadly means badly, so the letters of crime are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fuel stockpiles make crime unfortunately pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial venture is run for money, so the word can mean profit-making or financially viable.

clue.text: I see frames close to the picture

indicators.note: the word for see frames, surrounds, the closing letter

parts.note: to see someone is to date them

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone notices the frame round the edge of a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine or form an idea of it.

clue.text: 2016's arrival

parts.note: read as twenty sixteen: the answer at 20 is a commercial, an advertisement, and the answer at 16 a hole, an opening or outlet
the sixteen half points to the answer at 16, a hole, and an opening or outlet is a synonym for it

explanation.surface: The coming of a new year, 2016.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 2016 as 20 + 16: COMMERCIAL gives AD, HOLE gives VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means the coming or arrival of something notable.

clue.text: I cut start of race run during day

parts.note: the first lap is the start of a race

indicators.note: the run letter goes during, inside, the word day

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner boasts of cutting the opening lap of a race held during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of race' is not R but a whole LAP, the first one; 'run' supplies the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidary describes work engraved or cut into stone, and a lapidary is a gem-cutter.

clue.text: Hangover — need to bury head?

indicators.note: the phrase buries the answer inside its letters, concealed across two words

explanation.surface: Someone with a hangover wonders whether they need to put their head under something.
explanation.definitionFit: To head an organisation is to lead or rule it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Following cross, evidently a goal?

indicators.note: evidently, in plain view, a ball shaped like the cross letter is seen sitting inside the goal

parts.note: the net of a football goal stands for the goal
X is a cross-shaped letter

explanation.surface: A footballer's cross leads, it seems, to a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming immediately after, the one following.

clue.text: Without love, we ask person to be sad

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the word we goes around the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
to beg is to ask earnestly
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: Lacking affection, we plead with someone to be unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone means looking miserable or sorrowful, a close synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Unwilling to dress, skirts not needed

indicators.note: the skirts are the edges of the word, which are dropped

parts.note: to clothe is to dress

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to get dressed, saying skirts are unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth, also spelt loath, means reluctant or disinclined.

clue.text: First clue came up: Dry as air

parts.note: the sun rose, came up
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
tone is an air or character, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: A puzzle's opening clue turned up, reading like a weather report about dry air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone gave scholars their first key to Egyptian hieroglyphs, the breakthrough hint to decipherment.
